clue.text: It will support the architrave, you can count on it

definitions.meaning: in classical architecture the flat slab crowning a column's capital carries the architrave above it
a frame of beads on wires used for reckoning sums

explanation.surface: A builder reassures a client that a sturdy column top is utterly dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on it' sounds like an assurance of reliability, but it literally means doing arithmetic with the beads.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the slab on top of a column capital and the bead-frame calculator, a double sense.

clue.text: After the start, girl supports lad in hearing, showing resilience

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl's letters sit beneath the other piece, holding it up
in hearing means the word for lad is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: the girl's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl props up a boy, showing how resilient she is.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyancy is the ability to recover from setbacks, a cheerful resilience.

clue.text: Music-maker takes wine outside home

indicators.note: the wine goes round the other word

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means at home

explanation.surface: A musician takes a bottle out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet, a woodwind instrument, makes music.

clue.text: Salt, possibly, starts to improvise notes in shanty

indicators.note: the letters go inside the shanty

parts.note: a shanty is a sea song

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A sailor improvises notes in a chanty.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is an example of a seasoning added to food.

clue.text: Instrumentalist's record includes variation on tune

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the word for record takes the scrambled letters inside it

parts.note: to list is to record, and a list is a record

indicators.note: a variation on something rearranges it, so the letters of tune are reworked

explanation.surface: A musician's recording features a new version of a melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation on' rearranges the letters of 'tune' to UTEN; 'record' looks like a disc but is a verb-sense synonym for a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the lute, the plucked Renaissance string instrument, is an instrumentalist.

clue.text: Expect your setter to be so smartly dressed

definitions.text: Expect your setter to be so smartly dressed

parts.words: Expect your setter to be so smartly dressed
parts.note: the setter here is the dog breed, whose meal would be the reference point; the phrase is ironic slang for overdressed

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for flashily or showily dressed, often ironically.

clue.text: Mournful English member, one with a cold

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An Englishman with a bad leg and a cold is gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means sorrowful, in the manner of a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Fearless traveller carrying books, one I'd seen about

indicators.note: the pair of pieces goes round the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the contraction loses its apostrophe
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books
a rep, commercial traveller, sells on the road

explanation.surface: A traveling salesman lugs books about and is unafraid.
explanation.walkthrough: The traveller 'carrying' the books just joins them; 'seen' is a link too. The pair from 'one I'd' is split after its first letter to go about the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means bold and unafraid.

clue.text: American band a certain number found irritating

parts.note: tire is the American spelling of tyre, a rubber band round a wheel
some means an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A US rock group with some members is found annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians; it is a hoop of rubber round a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means annoying or tedious.

clue.text: Male warmonger carrying a fighting axe

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat
a hawk is a political advocate of war

explanation.surface: A belligerent man is seen bearing a battle weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The light axe of Native North American peoples was used as a weapon in combat.

clue.text: Speculator recovering from illness

definitions.meaning: someone who wagers money on an outcome
improved in health after being unwell

explanation.definitionFit: One who bets is a speculator, and someone feeling improved after sickness is said to be so.

clue.text: Obsession about larva over in Winnipeg area

indicators.note: the obsession word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a mania is an obsession

indicators.note: over turns the larva word back to front

parts.note: a bot is the larva of the botfly

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on grubs is found up in central Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the larva word into TOB; a bot is the grub of the botfly, a less familiar crossword stand-by.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian province whose capital city is Winnipeg is the area meant.

clue.text: Sundry ducklike birds

definitions.meaning: loons, diving waterbirds, are called this in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The word means various as an adjective and names the loons, diving waterfowl, as a noun.

clue.text: Serialised blockbuster about singular old woman

indicators.note: the film word goes round the other letters

parts.note: an epic is a lavish blockbuster film
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A big-budget film tells the story of a single elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something told in instalments or parts is episodic, as a serial is.

clue.text: Native beginning to chase antelope that's right outside

indicators.note: the letters go round the antelope piece

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

indicators.note: the first letter of chase is taken

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A local starts hunting an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the letters of 'that's right' around the rest, splitting after the first letter. 'Native' alone defines, so the country must be inferred.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iceland is the one meant, with the defining country left unstated.

clue.text: Flirted endlessly going over island

indicators.note: going over turns the shortened word back to front
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: toyed, as in toyed with someone's affections

explanation.surface: Someone flirted without stopping while crossing to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TOYED to TOYE, and 'going over' turns it to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ait or small island in a river, especially the Thames, is called this.

clue.text: Opt for having wealthy husband taken away and charged

parts.note: to elect is to choose or opt for

indicators.note: taken away removes that letter from the wealthy word

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A woman picks a rich husband and he gets taken away and charged with crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric means charged, carrying electricity, and also emotionally charged.

clue.text: For example, Zeus's bizarre main ploy

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: bizarre means the letters are put into a weird new order

explanation.surface: The king of the gods comes up with a strange main ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus is an example of the Greek gods who lived on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Force surrendering hill at end of battle

indicators.note: surrendering means giving up the word hill, which sits at the end of the battle's name

parts.note: Edgehill, in 1642, was the first pitched battle of the English Civil War
taken as written

explanation.surface: An army gives up high ground as a battle closes.
explanation.walkthrough: EDGEHILL was the first big battle of the English Civil War; 'at end of' shows where HILL is lost from.
explanation.definitionFit: Edge means sharpness or forcefulness, as in an edge to one's voice.

clue.text: Head of English upset over one's dotty marking

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter
over turns the word back to front

parts.note: to spill is to upset, as a drink
I + S, one with possessive

explanation.surface: An English chief is overturned with a mark of omission.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots marking an omission make the punctuation called this, so a dotted mark.

clue.text: Person running errands for a ruthless tycoon?

definitions.text: Person running errands for a ruthless tycoon?

parts.words: Person running errands for a ruthless tycoon?
parts.note: an errand-runner is told to go and get things, while the tycoon is an aggressively ambitious achiever

explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising, aggressively ambitious person, whose name also describes one who fetches things.

clue.text: Type of porcelain manufactured in layers?

parts.note: hens are layers, and what a laying hen produces round its egg is a fine brittle casing

explanation.surface: A kind of china is made in stacked sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' suggests strata, but means hens laying eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin, delicate translucent china is named after the brittle egg casing it resembles.

clue.text: Rings for reinforcement, mentioning detached territories

indicators.note: mentioning means the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: islets are small detached islands

explanation.surface: Reinforcing rings are mentioned in connection with outlying lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Small metal rings reinforce holes for laces in shoes or fabric.

clue.text: Wave when brother finally reaches end of valley

indicators.note: the letter arrives at the end of the valley word

parts.note: a combe is a short valley, especially in southern England

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of brother

explanation.surface: A wave appears when a sibling at last arrives at the far end of a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curling wave breaking on the shore is a comber.

clue.text: Dine out, entertaining wise men, it's supposed

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the wise men within them
out means the letters of dine are put out of order

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity

explanation.surface: Eating out while hosting wise men is what someone presumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of 'Dine' to INED; 'entertaining' places the wise men after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have imagined something is to have supposed or fancied it.

clue.text: One plundered property in Strathmore I've recovered

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Stolen goods taken from a Scottish estate have been found again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' looks like a reversal signal, but the run reads forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reiver was a Border raider who plundered cattle and goods.

clue.text: Knottiness impairing DIY? Not so

indicators.note: impairing damages the letters so they come out reshuffled

explanation.surface: A handyman is told that his tangled work is not spoiling the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impairing' rearranges DIY and NOT SO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodosity is the quality of being knotty or full of nodes.

clue.text: Sort of sugar kept back in container

indicators.note: the sugar word keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: caster sugar is fine granulated sugar

indicators.note: back means the little word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: A kind of sugar is stored at the back of a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IN to NI, and 'kept' places it in CASTER; caster is fine baking sugar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a small container, often for tea or sugar.

clue.text: Watering-place soldiers used, inter alios

indicators.note: Latin for among, so one piece goes among the letters of the other

parts.note: Latin for others, which is the rest
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops went to a spa town along with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alios' is Latin for 'among others': OR goes into REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering-place is a spa or seaside resort.
